account: On 3 November 2022 at about 5 pm, Madhya Pradesh's state cyber police received an alert emailed by Instagram's US office. It said that a user in the state had suffered a body injury. The Indore cyber-crime unit shared the “self-harm” alert with the cyber headquarters in Bhopal (ANI, 5 November 2022; Times of India, 4 November 2022). The girl, 17, had uploaded two videos. In one, a packet of poison lay beside her as she acted as if drunk. In the other she appeared to cut a vein (ANI). The Times of India notes a small cut on her wrist. Vaibhav Shrivastava, superintendent of police with the state cyber police, said: “After an effort of one hour, we traced the location of the girl”. She was in Satna district, whose police were informed (ANI). Ashutosh Gupta, the Satna superintendent of police, said that officers located her and called her in with her mother. She said that she only wanted to scare her boyfriend, and she was sent home after counseling (Times of India). In January 2026 Decode reported that Meta reviews flagged posts before it alerts police and that Meta publishes no data on false alarms. From its own interviews with Uttar Pradesh police, Decode also described a false alarm in Kanpur Dehat, where a student said that she had posted a video with tablets only to gain views.

ai_role.statement: Police say that the alert came by email from Instagram's US office after the videos were posted. An ASP described the platform's AI algorithms as flagging non-graphic self-harm content such as scars, search words and hashtags. Decode reports that posts reach police after AI systems or user reports flag them and Meta's staff review them, so the alert likely combined a classifier or a report with human review. No source says which started this alert. Everything after the email was police work. Bhopal and Indore technical teams traced the location in about an hour, and Satna police found and counseled her.

evidence.citation: Shefali Srivastava, Meta Flagged A Suicide Post. Police Had Minutes To Save The Man, Decode, 6 January 2026. The reporter has no tie to Meta or the police; she interviewed Uttar Pradesh officers and a psychiatrist about the same alert system and reports that Meta reviews flagged posts before it shares them, that some alerts are false alarms and that Meta does not publish error rates. The story does not cover the Satna case.
evidence.quote: Meta does not publicly disclose state- or country-level data on false positives in suicide-risk alerts shared with law enforcement.

fields.account: On 3 November 2022 at about 5 pm, Madhya Pradesh's state cyber police received an alert emailed by Instagram's US office. It said that a user in the state had suffered a body injury. The Indore cyber-crime unit shared the “self-harm” alert with the cyber headquarters in Bhopal (ANI, 5 November 2022; Times of India, 4 November 2022). The girl, 17, had uploaded two videos. In one, a packet of poison lay beside her as she acted as if drunk. In the other she appeared to cut a vein (ANI). The Times of India notes a small cut on her wrist. Vaibhav Shrivastava, superintendent of police with the state cyber police, said: “After an effort of one hour, we traced the location of the girl”. She was in Satna district, whose police were informed (ANI). Ashutosh Gupta, the Satna superintendent of police, said that officers located her and called her in with her mother. She said that she only wanted to scare her boyfriend, and she was sent home after counseling (Times of India). In January 2026 Decode reported that Meta reviews flagged posts before it alerts police and that Meta publishes no data on false alarms. From its own interviews with Uttar Pradesh police, Decode also described a false alarm in Kanpur Dehat, where a student said that she had posted a video with tablets only to gain views.
fields.summary: An alert from Instagram's self-harm detection led Madhya Pradesh police to a 17-year-old in Satna within about an hour on 3 November 2022, and she was counseled and sent home.

display.answer: The platform’s likely contribution was to prioritize concerning content for escalation, while police located the person and decided the response.

value.text: Instagram emailed a self-harm warning to cyber police, technical teams traced the account, and local officers brought the girl and her mother in for counseling.

purpose: Instagram's self-harm detection was built to flag content indicating self-harm or suicide risk and route alerts to agencies that can intervene. An alert that brought police to a girl posting self-harm videos was that purpose.

ratings.reason: A 17-year-old had posted videos with poison and an apparent cut. She was reached and counseled within about an hour of the alert and sent home with a small cut on her wrist. By her own account she wanted to scare her boyfriend. An averted suicide rests on the police's framing and is not established.

echoes.setting: Chhattisgarh, earlier: per ASP Vaibhav Srivastava, a previous Instagram “suicide” alert to the Madhya Pradesh cyber cell led to a girl being traced to Chhattisgarh and saved by local police

Uttar Pradesh, India: a Meta alert on 13 October 2025 led Unnao police to a 19-year-old who had already tied a noose, and the state police say that such alerts prevented 1,597 suicide attempts between January 2023 and November 2025; Decode also reports a false alarm in Kanpur Dehat

must_hold: The account's IP or other details resolve to a reachable district
The person is found before any act. Here she was found with a small cut on her wrist
A standing channel exists between Instagram and the state cyber police. This was the unit's second such alert
produced_by: Instagram's self-harm detection and alert routing, which per the police flags non-graphic self-harm content and emails state cyber police with account information
A state cyber police unit (Bhopal headquarters and Indore unit) able to trace the account's location from the emailed information, here in about an hour
District police able to reach the person and hold a counseling session with a parent present
